aboutHyperLayering.sectionBody:
At the heart of the Web is the hyperlink.

Content distributed around the world can be linked and referenced, without the need for centralization. This simple, open mechanism has enabled the Web to grow.

Hyper Layering extends this  concept to the way we combine information. Users can select information they need from different organizations and overlay it in their browser without  involving a central system.

Maps share a common coordinate system: latitude and longitude.

These shared coordinates allow information from different organizations and systems to be overlaid as layers within the same geographic space.

The Web contains a wide range of information about terrain, roads, buildings, weather, transportation, disaster preparedness, sensors, and local communities. By combining these layers on a single map, we can see the relationships between them that  would otherwise be difficult to understand from any one source alone.

A defining feature of Hyper Layering is that information used does not need to be consolidated into a single system.

With Hyper Layering, while information remains on the Web systems managed by its providers, users can select the layers they need and freely overlay them in their own browsers.

The underlying technology that enables this decentralized use of information is HLA (Hyper-Layering Architecture). HLMap (Hyper-Layered Map, formerly SVGMap) is a Web map viewer built on HLA.

Overlaying different kinds of information within the same geographic space reveals connections between sources that were previously separate.

Disaster information and evacuation facilities, weather and sensor data, transportation and people’s movements, local information and urban spaces: the information we choose and how we combine it can offer different perspectives on the same space.

aboutCloser:
Use information where it already resides, without gathering it in one place.

Overlay and combine layers to discover connections that were previously hidden.

This is Hyper Layering.
about:
Hyper-Layering Architecture (HLA) is an open architecture for combining independent content, data, and services on the Web through geographic space.

Hyper-Layered Map (HLMap) is a Web map viewer based on HLA. In autumn 2026, SVGMap was renamed HLMap to reflect the broader Hyper-Layering concept.

With HLA, each layer can be an independent source of content, data, or services. Instead of relying solely on information aggregated by a portal, users can freely choose and combine different sources and layers directly in their browser.

HLA is not merely a concept. It is a proven foundation technology that has been used for many years to integrate more than 200 Web-based systems as map layers.
